title: Microsoft Graph OAuth and QNAP Readiness Fix
goal: Fix the Pros Microsoft Graph OAuth user flow so browser OAuth can complete without a dead localhost callback or manual Node snippets, and verify QNAP MCP Assistant plus QNAP File Station readiness paths in the same setup surface.

included: Microsoft Graph and QNAP setup documentation
excluded: Changing Azure App Registration outside documented prerequisites
Persisting or printing real OAuth tokens, refresh tokens, bearer headers, QNAP tokens, or client secrets
Executing real QNAP writes/transfers without preview and explicit approval

apiContracts.rationale: The plan changes local CLI commands, OAuth callback handling, credential storage, MCP client configuration, and documentation. It does not introduce a frontend/backend or service API boundary.

analysis.tooling: Serena CLI fallback was used because Serena MCP calls were timing out/aborting in this session.
findings: microsoft-oauth.ts already contains createMicrosoftOAuthStart, completeMicrosoftOAuth, consumeMicrosoftOAuthSession, refreshMicrosoftToken, and revokeMicrosoftToken.
cli.ts exposes integrations auth microsoft-graph start and integrations graph status, but no obvious normal complete/callback command is exposed in help.
mcp-client-config.ts checks Microsoft Graph client ID readiness and QNAP MCP Assistant token readiness for managed MCP entries.
mcp-qnap-assistant.ts starts the bridge with token handling through environment/header mechanisms rather than command arguments.
qnap-files.ts already includes HTTPS endpoint, credential target, share allowlist, and preview/approval protections.

constraints: Reuse completeMicrosoftOAuth rather than duplicating token exchange logic.
Make the normal Microsoft OAuth path user-friendly and documented; do not require manual Node snippets for normal setup.
Keep all OAuth and QNAP credential handling redaction-safe.
Do not hardcode a specific Entra user; support tenant/client configuration generically.
QNAP writes or transfers must remain preview/approval guarded.

tasks.title: Document the current Microsoft OAuth localhost-refused failure
acceptanceCriteria: The localhost-refused failure is recorded as a product/UX bug.
The cause is clear: start prepares a localhost redirect URL without a visible normal listener or completion command.
Existing OAuth primitives are identified as reusable building blocks.

tasks.title: Decide the Microsoft OAuth completion UX
acceptanceCriteria: A listener-first or complete-command-first design is selected and documented.
Fallback behavior is defined for occupied port, browser launch failure, tenant/app mismatch, and state/session mismatch.
The design avoids user-specific hardcoding.

tasks.title: Implement official Microsoft OAuth callback completion path
acceptanceCriteria: OAuth can be completed through an official pros CLI path.
completeMicrosoftOAuth is reused for token exchange and credential storage.
Successful completion stores tokens only in the OS Credential Store.
Failure output is redaction-safe.

tasks.title: Update Microsoft OAuth CLI help and user guidance
acceptanceCriteria: Relevant help output shows the supported OAuth completion path.
start output clearly states the next user action.
The normal setup path no longer requires a manual node --input-type=module snippet.

tasks.title: Add Microsoft OAuth completion regression tests
acceptanceCriteria: Tests cover successful callback/code exchange with a mocked token endpoint.
Tests cover state/session mismatch and missing client ID.
Existing AADSTS700016 app/tenant classification remains covered.

tasks.title: Verify Microsoft Graph status and MCP configure after OAuth
acceptanceCriteria: pros integrations graph status reports a redacted ready/refresh/credential status after OAuth completion.
pros mcp configure opencode --include microsoft-graph remains secret-free.
Doctor/probe output identifies missing client ID clearly.

tasks.title: Verify QNAP MCP Assistant token and readiness path
acceptanceCriteria: pros mcp qnap token set/status/clear behavior is redaction-safe and documented.
QNAP MCP Assistant token is not placed in CLI args.
Missing-token readiness output is actionable.

tasks.title: Verify QNAP File Station fallback profile and allowlist behavior
acceptanceCriteria: HTTPS endpoint, credential target, profile selection, share allowlist, and preview/approval requirements are tested or confirmed.
Missing profile, missing credential, blocked share, and traversal cases return actionable errors.
No operation writes or transfers without explicit preview/approval.

tasks.title: Align QNAP Doctor and MCP status outputs with real setup expectations
acceptanceCriteria: pros mcp configure opencode --include qnap-mcp-assistant and status/probe outputs match credential expectations.
AnythingLLM/OpenCode entries remain command-only and do not contain secret values.
Outputs distinguish missing token, missing profile, and blocked path conditions.

tasks.title: Update Microsoft Graph and QNAP setup documentation
acceptanceCriteria: Docs describe the Microsoft Graph OAuth normal path and fallback path.
Docs describe QNAP MCP Assistant and QNAP File Station fallback separately.
Docs contain no secrets, tokens, or user-specific values.

tasks.title: Run credential redaction and secret-safety regression checks
acceptanceCriteria: No logs/configs expose access tokens, refresh tokens, bearer headers, client secrets, or QNAP tokens.
Existing redaction tests remain green or are expanded where needed.

tasks.title: Run targeted and release verification gates
acceptanceCriteria: Targeted Microsoft OAuth, CLI, MCP config, QNAP Assistant, and QNAP Files tests pass.
mise run release-check passes.
Any skipped live-provider checks are explicitly documented.

doneWhen: Microsoft Graph OAuth can be completed without a manual Node snippet.
The localhost-refused browser experience is eliminated or replaced by a clear official fallback.
Microsoft Graph tokens are stored only in the OS Credential Store.
pros integrations graph status and pros mcp configure ... microsoft-graph behave consistently after OAuth.
QNAP MCP Assistant token/status/configure paths are verified.
QNAP File Station fallback remains HTTPS, credential, allowlist, and preview/approval protected.

decisionLog.rationale: The fix spans CLI UX, browser callback handling, credential storage, MCP config, QNAP readiness, tests, and docs.
Token exchange and credential storage primitives already exist and should not be duplicated.
The user requested QNAP checks; existing QNAP paths should be verified and tightened rather than rebuilt unnecessarily.
No new cross-boundary API or service contract is introduced.
